[Intro: sweeping white noise, bubbling synth sequence]

[Section A: soft drum box enters, bass pulse]

[Melody 1: singing lead synth, slow vibrato]

[Section B: string-synth chords under the sequence]

[Melody 3: lead and strings together, fullest]

[Outro: noise sweep rises and falls, sequence fades]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 124 BPM, 4/4, C minor. Light, floating and steady, more glide than beat.

VOICE: None. The lead synthesizer plays the melody with a slow vibrato so that it sounds almost like a wordless voice.

INSTRUMENTS: A bubbling eight-note analogue sequence, a singing monophonic lead synth with portamento, lush string-synth chords with phasing, a soft vintage drum box (rim, hi-hat and a light kick), a pulsing bass, long white-noise sweeps, faint radio static.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, noise and sequence. 0:22 Section A, drum box. 0:44 Melody 1. 1:16 Section B. 1:38 Melody 2. 2:10 Break. 2:26 Melody 3, fullest. 2:58 Outro, noise sweep and fade to 3:28.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 1976 French electronic: warm analogue synths, heavy phaser on the strings, tape echo on the lead, wide and soft.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The lead melody entering at 0:44.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original imagined clean air from a Paris kitchen in 1976. Fifty years on the same sounds describe a layer of atmosphere people now measure with worry, and the piece stays calm on purpose.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Weightless, curious, serene, receding.
